frequency_question: What proportion of submitted nuclear cooperation agreements face a successful joint resolution of disapproval enacted into law?
membership_rule: Includes any peaceful nuclear cooperation agreement formally submitted by the executive branch to Congress for review under the statutory review period.
provenance_note: claims 25 cases from only 3 named (8.3x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 25 major agreements identified; zero successful joint resolutions of disapproval blocking a 123 agreement have ever survived a presidential veto or been enacted.
known_gaps: Excludes minor technical extensions that did not go through full congressional review cycles.
skeleton: Total formal 123 agreements submitted since the 1958/1974 amendments establishing the modern disapproval mechanism (~25 significant agreements), times the historical passage rate of successful veto-proof joint resolutions of disapproval.
validity_reason: The statutory framework of the Atomic Energy Act section 123 has remained stable for decades, though political polarization could theoretically alter legislative dynamics.
